subsystems.name: Transmitter
subsystems.role: generates a high-power, coded microwave signal to illuminate the target.

subsystems.name: Antenna
subsystems.role: forms a narrow beam and collects the returning echo.
parts: large parabolic dish (e.g. 70 m Goldstone, 100 m Green Bank)

subsystems.name: Receiver
subsystems.role: amplifies and digitises the extremely faint echo.

subsystems.name: Timing and frequency standard
subsystems.role: keeps transmitter and receiver phase-coherent for delay-Doppler processing.

subsystems.name: Signal processing and imaging
subsystems.role: converts the echo into range-Doppler images and physical parameters.

subsystems.name: Bistatic link
subsystems.role: separates transmitter and receiver to improve sensitivity and flexibility.

buildSteps.title: Select the site
buildSteps.detail: Choose a location with a clear horizon, low radio-frequency interference and stable ground.

buildSteps.title: Provide the antenna
buildSteps.detail: Build or repurpose a large steerable dish; the surface must be accurate to a fraction of the observing wavelength.

buildSteps.title: Install the transmitter
buildSteps.detail: Mount a high-power klystron or similar amplifier at the focus or in a nearby building, with power supplies and cooling.

buildSteps.title: Set up the receiver
buildSteps.detail: Place a cryogenically cooled low-noise amplifier at the feed, followed by downconversion and digitisers.

buildSteps.title: Establish timing
buildSteps.detail: Install atomic clocks or hydrogen masers and a GPS-based time transfer to synchronise transmitter and receiver.

buildSteps.title: Build the signal chain
buildSteps.detail: Connect transmitter, antenna, receiver and digitisers through a phase-stable distribution network.

buildSteps.title: Develop software
buildSteps.detail: Write or adapt delay-Doppler processing, ephemeris prediction and image reconstruction code.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and verify
buildSteps.detail: Observe the Moon, known asteroids and planets to confirm sensitivity, resolution and pointing.

buildSteps.title: Operate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Run observing campaigns, monitor system noise, and update hardware and software.

prerequisites.why: high gain is needed to transmit a narrow beam and catch the weak echo.
klystrons and traveling-wave tubes produce the hundreds-of-kilowatts signals that reach distant targets.
hydrogen masers provide the stability required for coherent delay-Doppler imaging.
fast digitisers and correlators handle the wide bandwidths and compute images.
JPL ephemerides predict target positions so the beam can be pointed correctly.
cryogenic amplifiers detect echoes as faint as a few photons per second.

pathway.milestone: bistatic radar using Goldstone and Green Bank characterizes near-Earth asteroids and supports planetary defence
pathway.unlocks: detailed shape, spin and near-surface density for deflection planning.

pathway.milestone: next-generation radar with phased-array transmitters and larger dishes increases sensitivity and target coverage
pathway.unlocks: routine imaging of smaller asteroids and deeper subsurface probing.

pathway.milestone: integration with optical and infrared surveys for rapid response to new discoveries
pathway.unlocks: fast characterization of potentially hazardous objects.

pathway.milestone: space-based radar or a lunar radar facility for uninterrupted viewing and deeper penetration
pathway.unlocks: global mapping of asteroid interiors and planetary subsurface exploration.
